# Steinbach City Council Reporting

> Independent, plain-language reports on what Steinbach City Council (Steinbach, Manitoba, Canada) has said and decided, organised by topic. Each report answers one question, credits what council does well, compares Steinbach with other cities, and links every quote to its moment in the official meeting video.

- Sources: the City of Steinbach's recorded council meetings on YouTube (2015-2026) and the published minutes; other cities' own published programs for comparisons.
- Quotes are verbatim from automatic transcripts; speakers are identified by hand. Council members, the mayor and city staff are named; residents are identified by initials only.
- Each report has an 'About this page' section saying what could not be confirmed.
- Council for 2026-2030 (sworn in Nov 3, 2026): Mayor Earl Funk; Deputy Mayor Susan Penner; Councillors Damian Penner, Bill Hiebert, Jake Hiebert, Ron Falk and Greg Carlos.

## Money, growth and planning

Taxes, budgets, housing, business and the city's long-term plans.

- [Taxes, spending and priorities: how does Steinbach pay its way?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/taxes-spending/): Council's priorities, five years of budgets, reserves and the five-year debt rule, and how Steinbach's tax rate compares with Brandon, Selkirk and Thompson. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Steinbach in 10 to 20 years: what has council planned?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/future-planning/): Growth to 35,000–45,000 people, the $215 million wastewater decision, annexation and neighbours, and the plans that exist and don't, compared with Brandon and Winkler. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Housing and development: keeping up with growth](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/housing-development/): Affordable housing, apartments versus single-family neighbourhoods, and who pays for growth, compared with Brandon and Niverville. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Business growth and investment: what has council done?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/business-growth/): The end of the economic development office, the industrial land squeeze, the Chamber's business tax and downtown rules, compared with Winkler, Morden and Portage. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [New neighbourhoods: do drainage, sidewalks and parks arrive on time?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/new-neighbourhood-services/): Lot grading, sidewalks, playgrounds and paving in new subdivisions, wells and septic on the city's edge, and who checks, compared with Brandon, Winnipeg and Calgary. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)

## Getting around

Traffic, highways and transit.

- [Traffic in Steinbach: what can council do, and what has it done?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/traffic-congestion/): Main Street and Highway 12 are provincial, but council has tools: traffic counts, cost-shared intersections and lobbying. What it has used, and what peers do. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [A bypass around Main Street? What council says and what the traffic study shows](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/main-street-bypass/): Council says traffic comes to Steinbach rather than through it. What the city's own traffic studies show and can't show, and how Yorkton, Portage and Winkler handled their highways. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 20, 2026)
- [Can Steinbach have public transit?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/transit/): Steinbach's only transit serves seniors and people with disabilities. What council has said about anything more, and how similar-size cities run transit. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)

## Safety, health and services

Flooding, policing, health care, homelessness and the look and feel of the city.

- [Sewer backups: what council said, and how Steinbach compares](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/sewer-backups/): Council's plan after the 2024 and 2025 sewer backups, its reasons for not going further, and what Brandon, Winnipeg, Toronto and other cities do. (Meetings Sept 2025 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Crime and policing in Steinbach](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/crime-policing/): The 18-officer RCMP contract, policing priorities, overnight security patrols and community safety officers, and how cost and crime compare with Winkler, Morden, Brandon and Portage. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Health and wellbeing: what can council do?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/health-wellbeing/): Doctor shortages, the mayor's recruitment task force, clinic space, recreation and wellbeing, and what councils in Niverville, Clarington and elsewhere do. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Homelessness in Steinbach: what's been done, and what could be](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/homelessness/): From The Bridge to the shelter zoning rules: what council has done, its reasons for not doing more, and what Brandon, Thompson and Lloydminster do. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)
- [Property standards: how does Steinbach keep rentals and yards maintained?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/property-standards/): The junk-and-weeds by-law, basement-suite safety rules and complaint-driven enforcement, compared with cities that license rentals. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Quality of life: noise, belonging, parks, recreation and arts](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/quality-of-life/): Noise enforcement, welcoming newcomers, flags and inclusion, green space, recreation and arts space, and how other councils compare. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026)

## Having your say, and how council works

How to get something from council, how it hears residents, and how openly it decides.

- [Advocating to council: what has worked, and what hasn't](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/): 164 requests over eleven years: what residents and groups asked for, what they got, how each council member responded, and a playbook for advocates. (Meetings Dec 2015 – Nov 2026 · Updated Nov 6, 2026)
- [Public notice and having a say: do residents' objections count?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/public-notice/): How residents hear about rezonings and variances, and how often their objections changed the result, compared with Brandon, Selkirk and Lethbridge. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Behind closed doors? How much of council's work happens outside public meetings](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/behind-closed-doors/): Do unanimous votes mean decisions were made in advance? Four tests on 103 meetings, closed committee and budget sessions, and how they measure up against the Municipal Act. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Recorded public deliberation on Steinbach City Council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/council-deliberation/): How often councillors state a position and give reasons out loud, across 527 decisions. Provisional and AI-coded, with the data and method. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 13, 2026 · Data: .xlsx)
- [Who moves council's public-hearing motions?](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/public-hearing-motions/): How many of the 203 motions after public hearings each council member moved and seconded, each listed with a plain summary and its moment in the video. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 19, 2026)

## Follow-up: what's still open

What the 2022–2026 term left unfinished, and practical steps for the council that follows.

- [Unfinished business: questions for Steinbach's outgoing councillors](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/action-list/): Promises, referrals and decisions from the 2022–2026 term that the public record leaves open, each with dated quotes and a question that can be answered with a date, a number or a document. (Meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026 · Updated Oct 14, 2026)
- [Serving Steinbach well: an action plan for council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/action-list/candidate-action-plan/): Practical steps drawn from these reports, written for candidates and now for the new council: open, reasoned decision-making first, then process and policy gaps by topic. (Based on meetings Jan 2022 – Sept 2026)

## 2026 election (archive)

What the candidates said before the October 28, 2026 election, with full transcripts.

- [2026 council candidates' forum: every question, every answer](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-forum-2026/): All 10 candidates' answers at the Chamber of Commerce forum, side by side and linked to the video, with the incumbents' answers checked against their council record. (Chamber of Commerce forum, Oct 15, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)
  - [the full forum transcript](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-forum-2026-transcript/)
- [Residents' election forum: what residents asked, and how four candidates answered](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/residents-forum-2026/): Residents' questions on housing, health, transportation and quality of life, with full answers from the four candidates who attended. (Residents' forum, Oct 7, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)
  - [the full forum transcript](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/residents-forum-2026-transcript/)
- [Candidates in writing: growth and housing, flooding, and public safety](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/candidate-interviews-2026/): All 10 candidates' written answers to SteinbachOnline on three issues, side by side, with record checks for the incumbents. (SteinbachOnline, Oct 7–15, 2026 · Updated Oct 16, 2026)

Sub-pages of the reports above (for example, the advocacy report's pages by council term and by council member).

- [Earl Funk: what they said and did when people asked council for something](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/members/earl-funk/): What Earl Funk said and did when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something, 2015 to 2026.

- [Jake Hiebert: what they said and did when people asked council for something](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/members/jake-hiebert/): What Jake Hiebert said and did when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something, 2015 to 2026.

- [Michael Zwaagstra: what they said and did when people asked council for something](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/members/michael-zwaagstra/): What Michael Zwaagstra said and did when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something, 2015 to 2026.

- [A playbook for advocacy groups](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/playbook/): A step-by-step playbook for advocacy groups approaching Steinbach City Council, drawn from eleven years of requests.
- [Every request, 2015–2026](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/requests/): Every request from residents and groups to Steinbach City Council, 2015 to 2026, filterable, with data downloads.
- [2014–2018: Mayor Chris Goertzen’s council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/terms/2014-2018/): What happened when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something in the 2014–2018 term.
- [2018–2022: Mayor Earl Funk’s first council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/terms/2018-2022/): What happened when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something in the 2018–2022 term.
- [2022–2026: Mayor Earl Funk’s second council](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/terms/2022-2026/): What happened when residents and groups asked Steinbach City Council for something in the 2022–2026 term.
- [The story by term](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/terms/): How Steinbach City Council's response to requests from residents and groups changed from term to term and year to year, 2015 to 2026.
- [What works, and what doesn’t](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/advocacy/what-works/): Which routes into Steinbach City Council, which evidence and which timing moved decisions, whether surveys count, and council's reasons for saying no.
- [Public Judgment & Deliberation Index (PJDI)](https://steinbachcitycouncilreporting.ca/council-deliberation/methodology/): The Public Judgment & Deliberation Index (PJDI) v1.0: a rubric for analyzing recorded public deliberation in Canadian municipal council minutes and transcripts.
